instructions: Pull the stems off the 4 guajillos and 2 anchos and shake out the seeds. Put the chiles in a bowl, cover them with boiling water and leave them for 20 minutes, until they're soft.
Meanwhile, cut the 2.5 lb chuck into 4 or 5 big pieces and pat them dry. Season them all over with 1 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown half the beef for about 3 minutes a side, until it's dark brown and lets go of the pan. Move it to a plate and brown the rest the same way. Turn off the heat.

Scoop out 3/4 cup of the chile soaking water, then drain the chiles. Put the chiles in a blender with the soaking water you kept, the can of beef broth, half the onion, the 4 garlic cloves, 1 chipotle and 1 tsp of the adobo. Blend until very smooth.

Pour the sauce into the Dutch oven over medium heat and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, a pinch each of cinnamon and cloves, the bay leaf, the remaining 1 tsp salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Put the beef and its juices back in the pot. Cover it with the lid and move it to the oven. Cook for 3 hours, until the beef falls apart when you push a fork into it.
Lift the beef onto a board and shred it with two forks. Fish out the bay leaf. Turn the oven down to 200°F.
Spoon the red fat off the top of the broth into a small bowl. Keep the broth warm over low heat.
Finely chop the other half of the onion and a handful of the cilantro. Shred the 8 oz Oaxaca cheese and cut the lime into wedges.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium with a spoonful of the red fat. Dip a tortilla in the broth on both sides and lay it in the pan. Cook it for 30 seconds, then flip it over.

Pile some cheese, beef, onion and cilantro on half the tortilla and fold it over. Fry it for about 1 minute a side, until it's crisp. Make the rest the same way, three or four at a time, and keep them warm in the oven.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lime.
Serve the tacos with small cups of the broth and the lime wedges.
method_notes: Both soften dried guajillo and ancho chiles, blend them into an adobo with garlic, onion, vinegar and warm spices, braise beef chuck in it until it shreds, then dip tortillas in the braising broth, fry them with cheese and beef, and serve the broth for dipping. The Daring Gourmet (the lead) soaks the chiles in boiling water, adds a chipotle, tomato paste, brown sugar, cinnamon, cloves and bay, simmers the sauce before the beef goes in and braises at 300°F for about 3 hours. RecipeTin Eats sears the beef hard, fries the paste in oil, adds chiles de árbol and fresh tomato, and skims the red fat to wipe the tortillas before frying. This one scales the lead to 2.5 lb for four, browns the beef first as RecipeTin does, and keeps the heat to one chipotle.
